state.case_summary:
A 40-year-old man presented with 1 week of difficulty voiding and was catheterized for urinary retention. Ultrasonography revealed a large prostatic mass, and his prostate-specific antigen level was 0.62 ng/mL (normal <4.0). He denied pain, fever, or abdominal distension. Physical examination was unremarkable, and complete blood count, routine chemistries, and tumor markers (CEA, CA19-9, CA-125, SCC antigen, CYFRA) were all within normal limits. Digital rectal examination revealed an enlarged prostate with palpable nodules and an ill-defined border. Pelvic ultrasound confirmed a heterogeneous prostatic mass. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a 5.5-cm heterogeneous lesion in the right prostate lobe, and cystoscopy raised suspicion for bladder invasion. Positron emission tomography–CT and colonoscopy suggested rectal invasion. A provisional diagnosis of prostatic sarcoma was made, and a transrectal needle biopsy was performed. The biopsy result was interpreted as either prostatic stromal sarcoma or prostatic stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential.

C. Gastrointestinal stromal tumor was excluded by lack of c
D. Solitary fibrous tumor was excluded by absence of stat6 nuclear positivity
E. None

root.label: Subacute Urinary Retention Syndrome with Prostatic Mass and Suspected Malignant Potential
supporting_facts: enlarged prostate with palpable nodules on digital rectal examination
heterogeneous prostatic mass on pelvic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging
excluded_candidates: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: less likely due to presence of palpable nodules and heterogeneous mass on imaging
Prostatitis: less likely due to absence of pain, fever, or abdominal distension
alarm_features: suspected malignant potential of prostatic mass

B1.label: Prostatic Malignancy
askable_discriminators: Does the patient have a history of prostate cancer in the family?
Has the patient undergone any recent trauma to the pelvic area?
requestable_discriminators: Imaging studies to rule out metastases

B2.label: Non-Malignant Prostatic Disorder
askable_discriminators: Does the patient have a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia or prostatitis?
Has the patient experienced any recent changes in urinary habits?
requestable_discriminators: Cystoscopy to rule out bladder pathology

B3.label: Other Causes of Urinary Retention
askable_discriminators: Has the patient experienced any recent neurological changes or symptoms?
Is the patient taking any medications that could contribute to urinary retention?
